title: Abstract group extension from an integer degree kernel
statement: Let G,M be groups, d:G→Z a surjective group homomorphism and s an element of degree one. Given f:ker(d)→M and T in M satisfying T f(u) T⁻¹=f(sus⁻¹), there is a unique homomorphism rho:G→M restricting to f and sending s to T. Explicitly rho(w)=f(w s^(-d(w))) T^d(w). This is a group-theoretic statement independent of schemes, sheaves, and their fundamental representations.

source.place: The abstract extension, first three paragraphs

proof.text: Every w has the unique decomposition u s^n, n=d(w). Induct on positive and negative integers to obtain T^n f(u) T^(-n)=f(s^n u s^(-n)). Multiply two decompositions to prove multiplicativity. The kernel and degree-one formulas are the cases n=0 and u=1,n=1. Any other homomorphism has the same values on every decomposition, proving uniqueness. This is already the complete proved Lean implementation in the attached upstream module.
